# Deep Research Intelligence Packet

## Cycle metadata

- Packet ID: `dr-20260929-1906-all-gravy-validation`
- Research system: `Codex web research`
- Started at: `2026-09-29 19:06 CDT`
- Completed at: `2026-09-29 19:09 CDT`
- Research scope: Validate four first-party All Gravy customer pages for named restaurant deployments, product scope, rollout status, and operating limitations.
- Queue item or vendor: `competitor:all-gravy`
- Methodology: First-party customer-page validation with enterprise-versus-pilot scope, operator-group identity, outcome-causality, and recency boundaries preserved. The homepage and resource index were used only for discovery.

## Executive result

- Pages reviewed: 6
- Candidate pages validated: 4
- Brand-vendor-product observations added or revised: 4
- Company/competitor profile observations added or revised: 0
- Conflicts found: 3
- Material takeaway: All Gravy publishes named restaurant evidence for Mildreds, The DRG, Wok to Walk, and Honest Burgers across frontline communication, learning, onboarding, compliance, knowledge access, and AI-assisted employee support. Three pages describe broad organizational use; Wok to Walk is explicitly a selected-location test with a global-rollout goal, so its 100-plus-site footprint must not be recorded as a completed deployment.

## Evidence observations

### Observation 1

- Brand: Mildreds
- Vendor: All Gravy
- Product or category: Employee communication, learning management, onboarding, compliance training, chat, and AI-assisted employee Q&A and quiz creation
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: enterprise
- Evidence type: customer story
- Confidence: 90%
- Confidence rationale: All Gravy's named customer page identifies Mildreds' Head of People & Vibe, states a 250-plus-employee scale, and describes concrete company-wide workflows and outcomes.
- Source title: Mildred's case study: how they run their teams on All Gravy
- Source URL: https://www.allgravy.com/cases/mildreds
- Publisher or source owner: All Gravy
- Published date, if known: Undated
- Accessed date: 2026-09-29
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Mildreds moved from a clunky, email-heavy toolset to one All Gravy app combining communication, LMS, and the employee starting journey; the page says compliance training that previously took days or weeks can be completed in hours, while an AI assistant answers questions and builds quizzes.
- Product-specific evidence: Communication and recognition feeds, chat, onboarding, LMS, compliance learning, AI answers, and AI-generated quizzes are explicit.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The source is vendor-authored and undated. It does not state the number of locations, implementation date, contract scope, or independent measurement of the reported time savings.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm current deployment scope and connected HR, payroll, or scheduling systems in a Mildreds-controlled source.

### Observation 2

- Brand: The DRG
- Vendor: All Gravy
- Product or category: Frontline employee communication and learning platform
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: enterprise
- Evidence type: customer story
- Confidence: 90%
- Confidence rationale: The page names The DRG's Head of People, gives a 1,500-employee scale, and describes consolidated communication and training use across a growing multi-brand restaurant group.
- Source title: The DRG case study: how they run their teams on All Gravy
- Source URL: https://www.allgravy.com/cases/the-drg
- Publisher or source owner: All Gravy
- Published date, if known: Undated
- Accessed date: 2026-09-29
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The DRG replaced a platform that suffered login, training-discovery, communication, and engagement problems with an All Gravy app combining messaging-style communication and short-video training in one place.
- Product-specific evidence: Internal communication, short-form learning, engagement, and vendor-supported feature development are explicit.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The DRG is a restaurant operator group rather than a single consumer brand. The vendor-authored page does not name the included brands, locations, rollout date, or quantitative engagement measures.
- Recommended follow-up: Map The DRG's current restaurant brands and confirm whether every brand and location uses the same All Gravy tenant and modules.

### Observation 3

- Brand: Wok to Walk
- Vendor: All Gravy
- Product or category: Frontline operational updates, structured onboarding, training refreshers, and manager/HQ completion visibility
- Relationship indication: pilot
- Deployment scope: pilot
- Evidence type: customer story
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: The named page quotes Wok to Walk's COO and explicitly says the company is testing All Gravy at a selected number of locations while considering a global rollout.
- Source title: Wok to Walk case study: how they run their teams on All Gravy
- Source URL: https://www.allgravy.com/cases/wok-to-walk
- Publisher or source owner: All Gravy
- Published date, if known: Undated
- Accessed date: 2026-09-29
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Wok to Walk is testing All Gravy at selected locations for operational updates, repeatable onboarding, training refreshers, and manager/HQ visibility; the page presents 500-plus employees and more than 100 restaurants as the intended connected footprint and alignment goal.
- Product-specific evidence: Central operational updates, structured onboarding, training refreshers, and completion visibility are explicit.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The page also uses rollout language, but its clearest status statement says selected-location testing and a hoped-for global rollout. The 500-plus-employee and 100-plus-restaurant figures therefore describe a target or company footprint, not a verified completed deployment.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm pilot locations, go-live date, evaluation criteria, and whether a global rollout was approved or completed.

### Observation 4

- Brand: Honest Burgers
- Vendor: All Gravy
- Product or category: Unified employee communication, knowledge and resources, onboarding, AI-assisted answers, and work-life-boundary controls
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: enterprise
- Evidence type: customer story
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: All Gravy's customer page names Honest Burgers' Head of Restaurant Systems, states a 400-employee scale, and describes daily use and whole-team onboarding and engagement.
- Source title: Honest Burgers case study: how they run their teams on All Gravy
- Source URL: https://www.allgravy.com/cases/honest-burgers
- Publisher or source owner: All Gravy
- Published date, if known: Undated
- Accessed date: 2026-09-29
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Honest Burgers replaced a seven-tool employee experience and the sunsetting Workplace by Meta with one All Gravy app for communication, knowledge, resources, onboarding, and AI-powered answers; the page says the team engages with it daily.
- Product-specific evidence: Communication, knowledge access, resources, onboarding, AI answers, and controls supporting off-hours disconnection are explicit.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The source is vendor-authored and undated. It does not state location count, implementation date, adoption percentage, which seven tools were displaced, or whether every listed capability is used at every site.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm current location coverage, integrations, displaced systems, and adoption metrics from an Honest Burgers-controlled source.

## Negative findings

- Candidate or claim: Wok to Walk has completed an All Gravy rollout across more than 100 restaurants and 500-plus employees.
- Pages checked: https://www.allgravy.com/cases/wok-to-walk
- Result: The page explicitly says Wok to Walk is testing All Gravy at a selected number of locations and is looking to roll it out globally. The larger figures are treated as company scale or rollout goals, not completed deployment evidence.

- Candidate or claim: All Gravy is a restaurant POS, payments, ordering, or loyalty system.
- Pages checked: All Gravy homepage, resource index, and the four customer pages.
- Result: The reviewed pages support employee communication, learning, onboarding, compliance, knowledge, and AI-assisted workforce workflows. They do not establish All Gravy as a transaction-system vendor.

## Source ledger

| URL | Source type | Accessed | Supports observation(s) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| https://www.allgravy.com/ | Product and customer overview | 2026-09-29 | Discovery only | Used to locate customer stories and understand product positioning; broad scale claims were not promoted as deployment facts. |
| https://www.allgravy.com/resources | Customer-story index | 2026-09-29 | Discovery only | Used to select four named restaurant pages; summaries were not treated as independent corroboration. |
| https://www.allgravy.com/cases/mildreds | Customer story | 2026-09-29 | 1 | Named 250-plus-employee restaurant deployment; vendor-authored and undated. |
| https://www.allgravy.com/cases/the-drg | Customer story | 2026-09-29 | 2 | Named 1,500-employee multi-brand operator use; brands and rollout measures undisclosed. |
| https://www.allgravy.com/cases/wok-to-walk | Customer story | 2026-09-29 | 3 | Explicit selected-location test; global footprint is a goal rather than completed scope. |
| https://www.allgravy.com/cases/honest-burgers | Customer story | 2026-09-29 | 4 | Named 400-employee use with concrete modules; vendor-authored and undated. |

## Research notes and inferences

- Inference: All Gravy competes in the hospitality frontline-employee experience layer rather than in core restaurant transaction systems.
- Inference: The customer evidence is strongest for communication, onboarding, learning, and knowledge access; AI capability claims are product-specific but still vendor-authored and lack independent outcome validation.
- Review instruction: Preserve Wok to Walk as a pilot until a later source proves broader deployment, and keep The DRG as an operator-group relationship unless its individual restaurant brands are explicitly mapped.
